Let’s talk about something that hits close to home— Chapter 10: The Personal Side—Fairness as a Daily Practice.
Sure, strong organizational systems matter, but here’s the thing: fairness really lives in the choices we make every single day. No matter your role or title, you’ve got the power to help create a fairer workplace.
So, what does practicing fairness look like, day in and day out? Well, it’s often the little things:
It starts with listening with empathy—especially when a colleague’s perspective is different from yours.
It’s about speaking up when you notice something unfair, even if it’s just a small moment others might overlook.
Sharing credit for wins and making sure you acknowledge everyone’s contributions goes a long way.
It also means taking a good look at your own biases, being open to feedback, and wanting to grow.
And, maybe most importantly, reaching out to support new team members or colleagues who might feel left out—offering them guidance or just making them feel included.
Let’s make it real for a second. Imagine you’re in a meeting, and you notice someone getting interrupted again and again. You could gently steer the conversation back to them. Or, if you’re in charge of assigning projects, you can make a point to spread out opportunities as fairly as possible.
And remember, fairness isn’t just about how you treat others—it’s about being kind to yourself, too. Everybody slips up. Learning to be fair is a journey, not a destination. When you model fairness, you invite others to follow your lead.
Over time, these everyday actions start to add up. Like ripples in a pond, they shape your team’s culture, little by little. When fairness becomes a habit we all share, the workplace truly transforms—from the inside out.
